disease_label_per_paper: Refractory catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome with myocardial injury, pulmonary hemorrhage, and cerebral infarct
presentation_summary: 36-year-old woman with triple antibody-positive primary APS presented with 4 days of left-sided nonpleuritic chest pain after conversion from warfarin to therapeutic LMWH while attempting conception.
Presentation showed troponin 6.0 mcg/L, lateral ST depression, regional wall motion abnormalities, and CT ground-glass opacity consistent with pulmonary hemorrhage.
Despite heparin plus dual antiplatelet therapy she had recurrent chest pain and developed transient left hemiparesis; brain MRI showed an acute right parietal infarct.
Three organ systems within a week led to probable catastrophic APS; she received methylprednisolone, IVIG, plasma exchange, and rituximab.
